newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil won't abandon CVRD sale - Cardoso.
newsitem.headline: Brazil won't abandon CVRD sale - Cardoso.

text.p: Brazil will press ahead with privatization of Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) because failure to do so could jeopardize the country's economic stability, President Fernando Henrique Cardoso said.
"We are going to continue making progress (towards selling CVRD), calmly and patiently, meeting all the legal requirements. We are not going to give up," Cardoso said in a ceremony.
As government lawyers sought to overcome injunctions that blocked yesterday's scheduled privatization, the president said the country could not afford a long delay to the sale.
"When things get too slow, they can lead the country to lose the possibility of benefiting from all that which is available to us today," Cardoso said.
Earlier, the president of the National Development Bank, Luiz Carlos Mendonca de Barros, declined to predict when the CVRD auction might take place.
In his speech, Cardoso said the sale of CVRD was an important part of his government's attempts to modernize the Brazilian economy.
"There comes a time when change imposes itself," he said. "We can't let these opportunities slip through our fingers," he said.

As the president spoke, government lawyers were awaiting a verdict from a high court judge on their request that one court in Brasilia be responsible for all cases involving injunctions against the CVRD privatization.
The measure would make it easier for the Brazilian government to deal with the injunctions, which have been issued by courts the length and breadth of the country.
